Twenty-one task-sized recipes. Each says when to use it, runs on `mediation_demo`
(except the cluster and latent-mediator recipes, which simulate their data), and links to the article that explains it. For a
one-page lookup see the [Reference Card](refcard.html).

These recipes need medfit 0.8.0 or later (recipes 18 and 19 need 0.9.0, recipe 20 and the native route in recipe 7 need 0.10.0, and recipe 21 needs 0.11.0). CRAN has 0.3.2, which lacks
`mediation_demo` and the native, joint and cluster functions; install from
GitHub or r-universe (see the [home page](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/#install)).

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
covs <- c("covariate1", "covariate2")
```

## 1. One-line mediation

*When:* one mediator, one outcome, a data frame, and you want an answer now.

```{r}
#| label: r1-med
res <- med(mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
           outcome = "outcome", covariates = covs)
quick(res)
```

More: [Getting Started](getting-started.html).

## 2. I already have `lm` fits

*When:* you fitted the mediator and outcome models yourself.

```{r}
#| label: r2-lm
fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
            mediation_demo)
x <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y,
                       treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
tidy(x, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
```

More: [Model Extraction](extraction.html).

## 3. Binary outcome

*When:* the outcome is 0/1. Fit the outcome with `glm()`; the `b` path and `c'`
are on the logit scale.

```{r}
#| label: r3-binary
fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
d <- mediation_demo
d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome))
fit_yb <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
              data = d, family = binomial())
xb <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_yb,
                        treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
paths(xb)
```

More: [Model Extraction](extraction.html).

## 4. Weights and robust standard errors

*When:* inverse-probability weights, or case weights for independent
observations. Pair them with `se_type = "sandwich"`; model-based standard errors
are not valid under inverse-probability weights. The sandwich (HC3) standard
errors treat the observations as independent, so they do not handle survey
clusters, strata or replicate weights.

```{r}
#| label: r4-weights
ps <- glm(treatment ~ covariate1 + covariate2, family = binomial(),
          data = mediation_demo)
p_t <- fitted(ps)
p_m <- mean(mediation_demo$treatment)
ipw <- ifelse(mediation_demo$treatment == 1, p_m / p_t, (1 - p_m) / (1 - p_t))
xw <- fit_mediation(
  outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  weights = ipw, se_type = "sandwich"
)
tidy(xw, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
```

More: [Getting Started](getting-started.html).

## 5. Two mediators in a chain

*When:* treatment, then mediator 1, then mediator 2, then outcome. Put every
mediator in the outcome model.

```{r}
#| label: r5-serial
fit_m1 <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_m2 <- lm(mediator2 ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             mediation_demo)
fit_ys <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + mediator2 + covariate1 +
               covariate2, mediation_demo)
xs <- extract_mediation(fit_m1, model_y = fit_ys, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        mediator_models = list(fit_m2))
c(chain = unname(nie(xs)), every_path = unname(nie(xs, type = "total")),
  total = unname(te(xs)))
```

`nie()` is the full chain `a d b`; `type = "total"` adds the paths that skip a
mediator. More: [Model Extraction](extraction.html).

## 6. Two mediators side by side

*When:* both mediators are driven by the treatment, neither by the other.

```{r}
#| label: r6-parallel
fit_m1 <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_m3 <- lm(mediator3 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_yp <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + mediator3 + covariate1 +
               covariate2, mediation_demo)
xp <- extract_mediation(fit_m1, model_y = fit_yp, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator3"),
                        mediator_models = list(fit_m3), structure = "parallel")
paths(xp)
nie(xp)
```

The effect is the sum of the per-mediator products. More:
[Model Extraction](extraction.html).

## 7. Treatment-by-mediator interaction

*When:* the outcome model has `treatment * mediator`. You get the four-way
decomposition (CDE, INTref, INTmed, PIE) at a reference mediator level
`m_star`.

```{r}
#| label: r7-interaction
fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_yi <- lm(outcome_int ~ treatment * mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             mediation_demo)
xi <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_yi, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = "mediator1", m_star = 0)
decompose(xi)
```

The native engine gives the same parts from model syntax (0.10.0 or later): write the
product as `treatment:mediator1`. The fit warns once that the global model test is
not available for a product of a regression target.

```{r}
#| label: r7-native
sem_i <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
   outcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2",
  mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich"
))
decompose(extract_mediation(sem_i, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                            outcome = "outcome_int"))
```

More: [Model Extraction](extraction.html), [the native product term](model-native.html#product-terms).

## 8. Many mediators with products

*When:* several mediators and a treatment-by-mediator term. The result is the
joint effect over the mediator block; bootstrap it with `joint_effects()`.

```{r}
#| label: r8-joint
fit_m1 <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_m2 <- lm(mediator2 ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             mediation_demo)
fit_yj <- lm(outcome_int ~ treatment * mediator1 + mediator2 + covariate1 +
               covariate2, mediation_demo)
xj <- extract_mediation(fit_m1, model_y = fit_yj, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        mediator_models = list(fit_m2))
boot_j <- bootstrap_mediation(
  function(theta) joint_effects(xj, theta)[["nie"]],
  method = "parametric", mediation_data = xj, n_boot = 1000, seed = 1
)
c(estimate = unname(nie(xj)), lower = boot_j@ci_lower, upper = boot_j@ci_upper)
```

More: [Methods and Formulas](methods.html).

## 9. Cluster-randomized trial

*When:* the treatment is assigned to whole clusters (schools) and the mediator
and outcome are measured on individuals. Formulas hold fixed effects only; the
engine adds the random cluster intercept.

```{r}
#| label: r9-cluster-data
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)
set.seed(2026)
J <- 40
n <- 10
cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n)
x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J))
v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)
u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)
cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl])
cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n)
mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school)
cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n)
```

```{r}
#| label: r9-cluster-fit
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)
xc <- fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat, treatment = "X",
                    mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school")
tidy(xc, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
decompose(xc)
```

With few clusters add `se_type = "kr"` (needs `pbkrtest`), and bootstrap whole
clusters for the product effects:

```{r}
#| label: r9-cluster-boot
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)
nie_of <- function(dd) {
  unname(nie(fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = dd, treatment = "X",
                           mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school")))
}
boot_c <- bootstrap_mediation(
  nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat, cluster = "school",
  n_boot = 200, seed = 123
)
boot_c
```

The warning, when it appears, counts the draws dropped as singular or
non-convergent refits; the interval uses the rest. The own and spillover split
is a large-cluster approximation, and the interval
evidence for the cluster bootstrap is for other designs; see
[Methods and Formulas](methods.html) and [Bootstrap Inference](bootstrap.html).

## 10. I use lavaan

*When:* you fitted the model as a structural equation model. The same
accessors apply.

```{r}
#| label: r10-lavaan
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)
syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + c_prime * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
"
sem_fit <- lavaan::sem(syntax, data = mediation_demo)
xl <- extract_mediation(sem_fit, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = "mediator1", outcome = "outcome")
tidy(xl, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
```

More: [Model Extraction](extraction.html).

## 11. A latent mediator, native engine

*When:* the mediator is a construct measured by several indicators, and you want
its indirect effect without first averaging the indicators into a score. The
mediator `eta` is not a column of the data; the model syntax defines it.

```{r}
#| label: r11-latent-data
set.seed(11)
n <- 400
X <- rnorm(n)
eta <- 0.5 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.9)
ldat <- data.frame(
  X = X,
  m1 = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),
  m2 = 0.8 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),
  m3 = 0.7 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)
)
ldat$Y <- 0.4 * eta + 0.2 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)
```

```{r}
#| label: r11-latent-fit
syntax <- "
  eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3
  eta ~ a * X
  Y ~ b * eta + cp * X
"
xs <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = ldat, treatment = "X",
                    mediator = "eta", engine = "native")
tidy(xs, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
```

`fit_sem()` fits the same syntax and returns the `SEMFit`. `mbco_sem()` tests the
indirect effect as the minimum of two likelihood-ratio tests, refitting with
`a == 0` and with `b == 0`:

```{r}
#| label: r11-latent-mbco
mbco_sem(fit_sem(syntax, ldat), "a", "b")
```

## 12. A nonlinear constraint or a longer chain, native engine

*When:* you want to fix the direct effect at the indirect effect (`cp == a*b`), or
test the indirect effect of a three-mediator-step chain, which is a product of
three paths. Constraints may be nonlinear in the labels.

```{r}
#| label: r12-nonlinear
base <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment
"
free <- fit_sem(base, mediation_demo)
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "cp == a * b"), mediation_demo)
rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b", "cp")], tied = coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")])
```

The tied fit has one more degree of freedom and its standard errors respect the
constraint. `anova(tied, free)` is the likelihood-ratio test of it. For a chain
`a`, `d`, `b`, `mbco_sem()` takes the paths and returns the minimum of the single-path
tests, referred to a chi-square with one degree of freedom (conservative when
several paths are zero):

```{r}
#| label: r12-chain
chain <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator2 + mediator1 + treatment
"
mbco_sem(fit_sem(chain, mediation_demo), paths = c("a", "d", "b"))
```

## 13. Joint significance for a binary or count outcome

*When:* the outcome is binary or a count and you want to know whether the mediated
path exists, without an outcome-scale effect. Test `a = 0` and `b = 0` separately
and take the larger p-value (conservative). Each test is a likelihood-ratio test
for a binomial or Poisson model and an F test for a Gaussian, Gamma or `quasi*`
model, whose dispersion is estimated.

```{r}
#| label: r13-setup
d <- mediation_demo
d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome))
```

```{r}
#| label: r13-joint
joint_test <- function(fit_a, term_a, fit_b, term_b) {
  one <- function(fit, term) {
    known <- fit$family$family %in% c("binomial", "poisson")
    col <- if (known) "Pr(>Chi)" else "Pr(>F)"
    drop1(fit, scope = term, test = if (known) "LRT" else "F")[term, col]
  }
  p <- c(a = one(fit_a, term_a), b = one(fit_b, term_b))
  c(p, joint = max(p))
}
fit_a <- glm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d)
fit_b <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             data = d, family = binomial())
joint_test(fit_a, "treatment", fit_b, "mediator1")
```

More: [GLM families](model-glm-families.html#joint-significance-test-for-the-indirect-effect).

## 14. Compare two native models

*When:* you want to know whether a path or a constraint is needed, on the native
engine. `anova()` is the likelihood-ratio test for nested `SEMFit`s; it refits
nothing. `glance()` gives AIC and BIC side by side.

```{r}
#| label: r14-compare
full <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment
", mediation_demo)
reduced <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1
", mediation_demo)
anova(reduced, full)
rbind(reduced = glance(reduced)[, c("npar", "chisq", "AIC", "BIC")],
      full = glance(full)[, c("npar", "chisq", "AIC", "BIC")])
```

The restricted model is the one with more degrees of freedom. A small chi-square
difference says dropping `cp` costs little.

## 15. A defined parameter and its interval

*When:* you want the indirect effect, the total effect or the proportion mediated
with a standard error and an interval, from one fit. Define each with `:=`; the
delta method gives the standard error.

```{r}
#| label: r15-defined
dfit <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
  total := cp + a * b
  pm := ab / total
", mediation_demo)
dfit@defined
confint(dfit)[c("ab", "total", "pm"), ]
```

The interval for `pm` is wide because a ratio is unstable when the total is small;
`bootstrap_mediation()` on the extracted object is the alternative.

## 16. Bound a variance or fix a path

*When:* a variance should not go below a floor, or a path is known. Write the
bound or the value in the syntax and read the diagnostics: an active bound means
the estimate sits on the edge.

```{r}
#| label: r16-bound
bounded <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + 0 * treatment
  outcome ~~ lower(2) * outcome
", mediation_demo)
bounded@diagnostics$active_bounds
round(coef(bounded)[c("a", "b")], 3)
```

`lower(2)` is above the variance the data want (about 1.2), so the bound binds and
is reported. `0 * treatment` fixes the direct effect at zero.

## 17. Check a native fit before trusting it

*When:* before you report a native fit. Read the diagnostics, then ask whether the
model fits when it has restrictions (`df > 0`).

```{r}
#| label: r17-check
chk <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ treatment
  mediator2 ~ treatment
  outcome ~ mediator1 + mediator2
", mediation_demo)
chk@diagnostics[c("status", "active_bounds", "improper", "sign_check")]
glance(chk)[, c("df", "chisq", "p_value")]
```

No active bound, no improper solution and a passing sign check mean the optimizer
is fine. The chi-square on 2 degrees of freedom is large, so the model leaves out
something the data contain (here, the covariance of the two mediators' residuals):
the fit converged, and the model is still wrong.

More: [Methods and Formulas](methods.html).

## 18. Fix exogenous covariates (`fixed_x`)

*When:* a native model with many covariates needs many parameters, or you want to compare with
lavaan's default `fixed.x = TRUE`. Since 0.15.0 a native fit fixes the means, variances and
covariances of the exogenous observed variables at their sample values by default (`fixed_x` left unset);
`fixed_x = FALSE` estimates them instead. Left unset, `fixed_x` resolves to the explicit
set of exogenous variables, so `glance()$fixed_x` names what was fixed.

```{r}
#| label: r18-fit
syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2
  ab := a * b
"
fixed <- fit_sem(syntax, mediation_demo)
free <- fit_sem(syntax, mediation_demo, fixed_x = FALSE)
rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b")], fixed_x = coef(fixed)[c("a", "b")])
rbind(free = sqrt(diag(vcov(free)))[c("a", "b")], fixed_x = sqrt(diag(vcov(fixed)))[c("a", "b")])
rbind(free = free@defined[, c("est", "se")], fixed_x = fixed@defined[, c("est", "se")])
```

The estimates, standard errors and the defined parameter `ab` agree to the digits shown.
What changes is how many parameters the optimizer carries:

```{r}
#| label: r18-glance
cbind(fit = c("free", "fixed_x"), rbind(glance(free), glance(fixed))[, c("npar", "df", "chisq", "fixed_x")])
```

The parameter count falls from 19 to 10 (the free fit also estimates the exogenous variances, covariances and means) while `df` and `chisq` stay put. `glance()$fixed_x`
lists what is fixed (`""` when nothing is). With `fixed_x`, the fixed rows stay in `tidy()` flagged
`fixed_x = TRUE`, with no standard error, and the log likelihood, `AIC()` and `BIC()` become
conditional on the fixed variables, so they differ from the free fit's.

```{r}
#| label: r18-compare
tf <- tidy(fixed)
tf[tf$fixed_x, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
tryCatch(anova(free, fixed), error = function(e) cat(conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
```

Compare fits only when they fix the same variables. `anova()`, `mbco_sem()` and `AIC()`/`BIC()`
across several fits stop when the fixed sets differ, as above. Pass a character vector (for
example `fixed_x = "treatment"`) to fix a subset.

Since 0.15.0 the default is to fix the exogenous observed variables; pass `fixed_x = FALSE` to
keep the free exogenous block. See [the 0.15.0 defaults](native-defaults-0-15.html).

More: [Methods and Formulas](methods.html), [the native engine guide](native-guide.html).

## 19. Observed intercepts and means

*When:* you want the intercepts of a native model, or a test of whether an intercept is
zero. Since 0.15.0 every native fit has a mean structure by default (`meanstructure` left
unset is `TRUE`): an intercept is free for every observed variable you did not mention, as
lavaan does with `meanstructure = TRUE`. Writing an intercept (`outcome ~ 1`) is only needed to
restrict it. The paths and their standard errors do not change.

```{r}
#| label: r19-free
paths <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment
"
free <- fit_sem(paths, mediation_demo)
tf <- tidy(free)
tf[tf$op == "~1", c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
```

The outcome and mediator intercepts equal the `lm()` intercepts of the same equations.
The mean of `treatment` is the sample mean, fixed with the other exogenous moments, so its row has no
standard error. Writing `outcome ~ 1` in the syntax returns the same fit, because the default already
estimates that intercept.

A fixed intercept is a restriction. `outcome ~ 0*1` costs one degree of freedom and
changes the other estimates, so `anova()` can test it:

```{r}
#| label: r19-zero
zero <- fit_sem(paste0(paths, "outcome ~ 0*1"), mediation_demo)
round(c(free = free@theta[["cp"]], fixed_at_zero = zero@theta[["cp"]]), 3)
anova(free, zero)
AIC(free, zero)
```

The test rejects zero, and the restricted model has the larger AIC. A fit with
the mean structure off has no intercepts to restrict.

Pass `meanstructure = NULL` to fit a mean structure only when the model writes `~1` or a product (the
0.14.x rule), or `meanstructure = FALSE` for covariances only. See
[the 0.15.0 defaults](native-defaults-0-15.html).

More: [Native engine, intercepts](model-native.html#intercepts).

## 20. Four-way decomposition from a native fit

*When:* the outcome depends on the treatment, the mediator and their product, and you want
the controlled direct effect, the two interaction terms and the pure indirect effect. Write
the product as `treatment:mediator1` in the outcome equation, fit with `fit_sem()`, and
extract. A product needs the mean structure (on by default; `meanstructure = FALSE` is an error), so the covariate in the mediator equation
enters the reference interaction through its sample mean. The fit warns that the global
test is not valid with a product and recommends the sandwich covariance; the chunk
silences the warning and asks for the sandwich. A factor covariate (for example a `group` column in
the mediator equation) is expanded to dummies and enters the same way; a factor treatment or
mediator is not supported, so recode a two-level factor as 0/1 first.

```{r}
#| label: r20-fit
four_way <- "
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate2
  outcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1 + covariate2
"
fit20 <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(four_way, mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich"))
fw20 <- extract_mediation(fit20, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                          decomposition = "four_way")
tidy(fw20, type = "components", conf_int = TRUE)
```

The components sum to the natural direct and indirect effects, and `m_star` moves the
reference level of the mediator (default 0), which shifts weight between the controlled
direct effect and the reference interaction.

The standard errors treat the covariate mean as fixed, so they are conditional on the
observed covariates and slightly too small for a population average. To add the variance of
the estimated covariate mean to INT~ref~, the NDE and the TE, set the option below (the default
stays conditional, as lavaan's `:=` is); the other components do not change:

```{r}
#| label: r20-popse
op <- options(medfit.covariate_mean_variance = TRUE)
tidy(fw20, type = "components")[, c("term", "std_error")]
options(op)
```

On `mediation_demo` the added term is about 0.08% of the INT~ref~ standard error, so the table
matches the one above to the digits shown; it matters when the interaction and the effect of the covariate
on the mediator are both large (chapter 7 has a simulated case: 0.0995 becomes 0.1516
against a bootstrap SD of 0.1568).

The other route is the nonparametric bootstrap, which refits the model on each resample:

```{r}
#| label: r20-boot
int_ref_stat <- function(dat) {
  f <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(four_way, dat))
  extract_mediation(f, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                    decomposition = "four_way")@int_ref
}
boot20 <- bootstrap_mediation(int_ref_stat, method = "nonparametric",
                              data = mediation_demo, n_boot = 200, seed = 1)
c(estimate = boot20@estimate, lower = boot20@ci_lower, upper = boot20@ci_upper)
```

More: [Native engine book, the four-way chapter](https://github.com/Data-Wise/medfit/tree/main/book/chapters/07-four-way.qmd),
[Native engine, product term](model-native.html).

## 21. A categorical covariate in a native fit

*When:* a covariate is a factor, character or logical column (a group, a site, a yes/no flag).
Write the column name where a numeric covariate would go. The engine replaces it with one 0/1 dummy per
non-reference level, named `<column>_<level>`; the reference is the first factor level (a character column
sorts in the C locale). The rows of the fit are named `mediator1~group_mid`, so read them like any other
path. The chunk cuts `covariate1` into three groups to have a factor to use.

```{r}
#| label: r21-fit
dat21 <- transform(mediation_demo,
                   group = cut(covariate1, c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, Inf), labels = c("low", "mid", "high")))
fit21 <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a*treatment + group
  outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment + group
  ind := a*b
", dat21)
tidy(fit21)[1:7, ]
```

The estimates equal a fit with the dummies written by hand (`group_mid`, `group_high`), and `a`, `b` and
`ind` keep their usual meaning. A label goes on one dummy, never on the factor: `b*group` stops with a
message that names the dummies. To test one dummy, label it and constrain the label:

```{r}
#| label: r21-label
fit21b <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a*treatment + group
  outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment + group + z*group_mid
  z == 0
", dat21)
tidy(fit21b)[grepl("group", tidy(fit21b)$term, fixed = TRUE), ]
```

`fixed_x = "group"` fixes every dummy of the factor at its sample moments, and a dummy name fixes one:

```{r}
#| label: r21-fixed
fit21c <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a*treatment + group
  outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment + group
", dat21, fixed_x = "group")
generics::glance(fit21c)$fixed_x
```

Limits: a factor as an outcome or a mediator, an ordered factor, and a product of two factors are refused
with a message that says why; `group:mediator1` expands to one product per dummy. A bootstrap that refits from
raw data re-expands the factor in each resample, so a level missing from a character column's resample
changes the reference level.

More: [Native engine, paths and defined parameters](model-native.html), `?"medfit-syntax"`
(section Factor covariates).
